events.event_title: US-China Tariff Escalation & Trade War Re-ignition
events.event_description: The Trump administration has reimposed and escalated tariffs on Chinese goods, with China retaliating. This creates immediate supply chain disruption pressures, reshoring incentives, and margin compression for importers while benefiting domestic manufacturers and logistics rerouting plays.
events.rationale: POWL (Powell Industries) benefits from domestic electrical equipment manufacturing reshoring demand. ARCB (ArcBest) captures rerouted freight as supply chains shift away from trans-Pacific. KTOS (Kratos Defense) benefits from US-China tension driving defense spend. CEVA (semiconductor IP licensing) faces headwinds from Chinese customer exposure. APPS faces risk from China-adjacent app monetization channels tightening.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break below $8.20 with volume on tariff escalation news; or wait for RSI compression below 70 after pullback
tickers.exit_condition: Exit long if tariff negotiations signal de-escalation; exit short if APPS stabilizes above $9.00 on domestic monetization pivot announcement
tickers.risk: APPS has diversified away from China-dependent revenue; overbought RSI (84.6) suggests limited upside on this thesis; trade war narrative may not materially impact app monetization model; mean reversion risk on momentum play

tickers.entry_trigger: Break below $48.50 on volume with RSI divergence below 70; or wait for pullback to 20-day MA (~$47.80) if tariff escalation headlines intensify
tickers.exit_condition: Exit long if tariff news reverses (deal signals) or CEVA breaks below $46; exit short if breaks above $52 with RSI confirmation. Cut losses at >8% adverse move given event volatility.
tickers.risk: High RSI overbought conditions suggest limited downside room; tariff escalation may surprise positively for semiconductor IP licensing (China forced to license US tech). CEVA has limited direct China revenue exposure vs peers—thesis weakness. Sentiment whipsaw on trade deal headlines.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $305 on volume >500K shares with tariff escalation headlines, or dip to $285-290 on sector rotation weakness for accumulation
tickers.exit_condition: Tariff negotiations pause/reversal announcement, or RSI >65 without fundamental catalyst follow-through, or close below $280
tickers.risk: Trade war rhetoric fades faster than expected; POWL's supply chain still tied to Chinese components; margin compression outpaces demand lift; stock already priced in some reshoring benefit

events.event_title: NATO Defense Spending Surge & European Rearmament
events.event_description: Europe is rapidly accelerating defense budgets following continued Russia-Ukraine conflict and US pressure to reduce NATO reliance on American forces. Multiple European nations are committing to 3%+ GDP defense spending. US defense contractors with NATO interoperability products and ammunition suppliers face direct near-term contract catalysts.
events.rationale: KTOS specializes in drone and autonomous systems with NATO-compatible platforms seeing direct contract flow. CACI provides intelligence and C2 systems being rapidly procured. VEC (Vectrus/V2X) handles base operations and logistics for NATO installations. PLTR's Maven Smart System and European government contracts are accelerating. These are mid-cap names with direct program exposure versus mega-caps like LMT or RTX already priced in.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $60.50 resistance with volume >2M shares on NATO spending announcement or quarterly earnings beat on international/European revenue growth
tickers.exit_condition: Exit 50% at $68-70 (profit-take), trailing stop at $55 for remaining position. Full exit if NATO spending surge delays >8 weeks or fails to convert to actual KTOS contracts within guidance
tickers.risk: KTOS faces execution risk converting geopolitical tailwinds into realized revenue; 4-12 week timeframe may be too compressed for contract awards. Valuation already reflects defense spending narrative (RSI 60.3). Competition from mega-caps (RTX/LMT) undercutting on price/scale. Geopolitical de-escalation or peace negotiations collapse thesis entirely.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $535 on volume >2M shares with positive earnings revision or NATO contract announcement catalyst within 2 weeks
tickers.exit_condition: RSI >75 or failure to hold $520 support on close; take profits at $555 if event catalyst executes early
tickers.risk: RSI already elevated at 63.8 limits upside room before pullback; geopolitical deescalation narrative could deflate defense spending urgency; mega-cap defense contractors (LMT, RTX, NOC) may capture majority of NATO procurement; CACI's intelligence/C2 exposure less direct than drone/autonomous players (KTOS, PLTR)

events.event_title: AI Power Infrastructure Bottleneck & Data Center Energy Crisis
events.event_description: Hyperscaler AI buildouts are creating acute shortages in power transformers, switchgear, and grid interconnection equipment. Utility interconnection queues stretch years. This is a multi-quarter earnings catalyst for niche electrical infrastructure suppliers, not the chip names. Near-term earnings beats expected from backlog conversion.
events.rationale: POWL (Powell Industries) makes custom switchgear and has a record backlog converting to revenue now — direct earnings catalyst. MYRG (MYR Group) is an electrical construction contractor building out data center power infrastructure with strong order intake. GVP (MDU Resources spin-off exposure) captures utility construction. These are the picks-and-shovels behind the picks-and-shovels — less covered than Nvidia or Eaton, with cleaner near-term revenue visibility.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $305 on volume >500k shares with confirmation of Q next earnings beat or backlog conversion acceleration announcement
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $290 or earnings miss on backlog-to-revenue conversion; take profits at $330+ if AI power infrastructure narrative stalls or utility capex guidance softens
tickers.risk: Backlog conversion delays due to supply chain/labor constraints; utility interconnection queue timelines prove longer than expected; multiple compression if broader rate concerns resurface; execution risk on custom switchgear manufacturing ramp

tickers.entry_trigger: WATT breaks above $29.50 on volume >2M shares with positive wireless power news OR enters on 3-5% dip to $27-28 if broader infrastructure thesis accelerates
tickers.exit_condition: Exit 50% at +15-20% gain; trail stop on remainder at 8% below highest close. Hard exit if company misses guidance or wireless power adoption delays materialize
tickers.risk: WATT is wireless power play, not grid infrastructure—thesis mismatch with POWL/MYRG. Execution risk on commercial adoption. Stock underperforms if data center power capex delays or utilities slow interconnection spending. Liquidity concern with <1M avg daily volume.

events.event_title: GLP-1 Drug Demand Reshaping Adjacent Healthcare Markets
events.event_description: Ozempic/Wegovy/Mounjaro adoption continues to surge, creating second-order disruptions across medical devices (fewer bariatric surgeries, less knee replacement demand) while boosting demand for injection delivery systems, cold-chain logistics for biologics, and companies supplying API or fill-finish manufacturing capacity.
events.rationale: STVN (Stevanato Group) makes drug delivery systems and glass vials — direct GLP-1 supply chain beneficiary with capacity expansion underway. OMCL (Omnicell) sees pharmacy automation demand rise as GLP-1 prescription volumes stress hospital dispensing. ESTA (Establishment Labs) faces bearish pressure as body contouring procedures decline with weight loss drug adoption. NTRA (Natera) is insulated as a genetic testing play unaffected by GLP-1 but benefits from broader healthcare spend reallocation. INVA holds royalties on drug delivery mechanisms potentially applicable to GLP-1 formulations.

tickers.entry_trigger: INVA breaks above $23.50 on volume >2M shares with announcement of new GLP-1 delivery royalty agreement or capacity expansion; alternatively wait for RSI mean reversion above 45 during broader biotech rally
tickers.exit_condition: Exit if INVA closes below $20.80 (break of recent support); take profits at $26-27 on any GLP-1-related news catalyst; exit if competing royalty holders announce similar deals that dilute INVA's value capture
tickers.risk: Royalty income is backward-looking and small relative to stock price—GLP-1 tailwinds may already be priced in; INVA's delivery tech may be peripheral to actual GLP-1 formulation economics; execution risk on royalty recognition; broader biotech selloff could override event thesis

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $19.20 on volume >2M shares with earnings beat or capacity expansion announcement; or pullback to $17.80 on GLP-1 supply chain confirmation
tickers.exit_condition: RSI >70 + reversal candle; or close below $17.50; or macro pivot away from GLP-1 adoption narrative; or 16-week timeframe expires without catalyst confirmation
tickers.risk: Valuation already pricing in GLP-1 tailwinds; competition from alternative delivery systems (autoinjectors, pens); pharma customer margin compression; China capacity competition; macro downturn reducing biotech CapEx spending

tickers.entry_trigger: ESTA breaks below $68.50 on volume >2M shares as cosmetic procedure bookings guidance declines; short entry near resistance at $74.50
tickers.exit_condition: Close above $76 on earnings beat or GLP-1 adoption slowdown narrative shifts; take profit at $65 if thesis triggers within 8 weeks
tickers.risk: GLP-1 adoption may plateau before materially impacting elective cosmetic demand; ESTA could pivot to non-invasive body contouring products; short squeeze risk if fund rebalancing occurs
